paragraphs: Friend, here's what this chapter teaches me: shortcuts to a good thing don't make the shortcut good. Rechab and Baanah figured they were handing David a gift. They said, "Today the LORD has granted vengeance to my lord the king against Saul and his offspring." (2 Samuel 4:8) They used the LORD's name to dress up what they did, and David wasn't buying it.

David had a clear answer, and it came from where he'd been. He says the LORD "has redeemed my life from all distress." (2 Samuel 4:9) I think that's why he didn't need anybody's blood to get ahead. He tells them wicked men killed "a righteous man in his own house and on his own bed." (2 Samuel 4:11) You can want what God has promised and still refuse a road God never opened, friend.

So here's the question for your own kitchen. Where are you tempted to hurry something along and call it God's timing? Maybe it's a promotion, a deal or a win you could grab if you just cut one corner. This is a heavy chapter, and I think it hurts, but it points us to the better way: wait on the LORD, keep your hands clean, and let Him do the baking. The story isn't over, so keep your apron on.
